root_cause.text: The EROFS directory parsing code in `fs/erofs/dir.c` failed to validate trailing dirent `nameoff` values before using them in `strnlen()`, allowing `maxsize - nameoff` to underflow and read past the directory block, and it also did not enforce that `de[0].nameoff` was a valid multiple of `sizeof(struct erofs_dirent)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes trailing-dirent handling from unconditional `strnlen(de_name, maxsize - nameoff)` to first rejecting `maxsize <= nameoff` (`goto err_bogus`), and it adds the note that “trailing dirents are special since the namelens are calculated with strnlen() with unchecked nameoffs”; it also tightens `erofs_readdir()` validation from `nameoff < sizeof(struct erofs_dirent) || nameoff >= bsz` to `!nameoff || nameoff >= bsz || (nameoff % sizeof(*de))`, matching the CVE description that `nameoff0` must be aligned.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten EROFS directory entry validation to correctly reject bogus or malformed dirents, including invalid trailing entries and non-positive name lengths.
intent_record.what: The code changes the dirent length calculation logic in `erofs_fill_dentries()`: for non-trailing entries it now uses `de[1].nameoff - nameoff` when `de + 1 < end`, while for trailing entries it first checks `maxsize <= nameoff` and jumps to `err_bogus` before calling `strnlen()`. The validation check is also replaced: instead of separately checking `nameoff + de_namelen > maxsize` and `de_namelen > EROFS_NAME_LEN` with an error print and `return -EFSCORRUPTED`, it now rejects entries when `de_namelen` is not in the range `1..EROFS_NAME_LEN` or when `nameoff + de_namelen > maxsize`, and then jumps to `err_bogus`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, malformed directory entries are detected more robustly. The new logic prevents computing a name length from an invalid trailing offset, rejects zero or negative-looking name lengths as corrupted, and routes all bogus-entry cases through the same error path. This reduces the chance of accepting invalid on-disk directory data or miscomputing lengths that could lead to incorrect directory iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add explicit corruption handling for bogus EROFS directory entries by logging, asserting, and returning -EFSCORRUPTED.
intent_record.what: A new error label `err_bogus` was added at the end of `erofs_fill_dentries()`, which logs "bogus dirent @ nid %llu" using `EROFS_I(dir)->nid`, triggers `DBG_BUGON(1)`, and returns `-EFSCORRUPTED`.
intent_record.how: If directory entry parsing reaches the bogus-dirent path, the function now explicitly reports corruption, triggers a debug assertion, and fails the readdir fill operation with an on-disk corruption error instead of continuing normally.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten EROFS directory entry validation to reject zero, out-of-range, and misaligned name offsets as corrupted metadata.
intent_record.what: In erofs_readdir(), the validation for de->nameoff was changed from checking only that it was at least sizeof(struct erofs_dirent) and less than bsz to checking that it is nonzero, less than bsz, and aligned to sizeof(*de) via a modulo test.
intent_record.how: At runtime, directory entries with a zero name offset, an offset beyond the block size, or a misaligned offset are now rejected as corrupted, preventing the readdir logic from accepting malformed directory entry layouts.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff introduces the directory parsing logic and contains the vulnerable pattern. In `erofs_fill_dentries()` it iterates dirents and computes name length with `strnlen(de_name + de->nameoff, maxsize - de->nameoff)`. There is no validation that `de->nameoff` is within bounds before this subtraction, so a bad trailing `nameoff` could underflow `maxsize - de->nameoff` and make `strnlen()` read past the block. The code also only checks alignment of the current entry with `if (de->nameoff % sizeof(struct erofs_dirent)) return -EIO;`, but there is no check that `de[0].nameoff` itself is a valid multiple/starting offset constraint for the trailing dirent layout described in the root cause. Since the vulnerable logic is present and no fix is present in this commit, this is bug-introducing.
